observations: Job status per row is a colored pill badge (`.badge failed/running/succeeded` with a status dot) plus the capitalized word — visible on all 8 rows in idle_desktop; metrics count 29 badge-heuristic elements and 14 inline SVGs.

Job progress is a div-based fill bar (`.progress-fill` colored by status) plus a numeric percent ('38%', '81%', '100%') in every row, and the upload panel has its own `.upload-progress-fill` bar with live % — though metrics show progress=0, meter=0, roleProgressbar=0, so no native/ARIA progressbar semantics back the visuals.

Queue-level counts are five cards whose values are color-coded to the status system (purple QUEUED 0, blue RUNNING 3, green SUCCEEDED 2, red FAILED 3) and show colored skeleton dashes while loading (loading_desktop shot); color is the only graphical channel — no bar or trend glyph.

Failure reason is red text only ('Worker ran out of memory at 1.8 GB', 'Upstream timeout after 30s' in the DETAILS column, `.error-text` with a title tooltip); severity is signaled graphically by the adjacent red Failed badge, but the reason itself has no icon in the row.
Raw ratio: 3/4 inventory items graphical+text, 1/4 text only.
Measured desktop viewportWords is 95 for a full dashboard (header, 5 cards, 5 filters, 8-row table) — nearly every word is data, not prose.
helperWords = 0 and longLeafWords = 0: there is not a single explanatory paragraph or >12-word leaf string on the page.
12 button labels, meanWords 1.17, maxWords 3, longLabels empty — 'Retry', 'Cancel', 'All', 'Upload & Process' are the longest labels.
The only instructional sentence is 'Drop a file or browse' in the dropzone, which carries real instruction; toasts ('Job requeued', 'Job cancelled') are 2 words and state results, not narration.
Nothing restates what the UI shows: the counts, badges, and bars stand alone with single-word labels (TOTAL, QUEUED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED).
Status vocabulary is perfectly consistent across four surfaces: summary cards, filter tabs, row badges, and the upload panel's final 'Queued' step all use Queued/Running/Succeeded/Failed.

Copy matches observed behavior: 'Upload & Process' does exactly uploadFile→processFile; 'Live' is backed by observed 3 s listJobs polling (async item 8 PASS); 'Connection issue — retrying automatically' is literally true since the poll interval keeps running.
Failure reasons and errors are specific, not filler: 'Worker ran out of memory at 1.8 GB', 'Network error — check connection', 'Retry failed: ' + e.message.
One micro-issue found (redundancy in a toast), which keeps this just under the no-issues anchor; no marketing tone, no placeholder text, no false promises anywhere.

The interaction design is unmistakably shaped by 'deal with failed jobs': renderTable sorts failed→running→queued→succeeded so all three failed rows with reasons and Retry buttons sit at the top of the table, and FAILED has its own filter tab and red count card.
Actions are status-contingent per row — Retry only on failed, Cancel only on running/queued, 'Download (2,713 rows)' only on succeeded — which is job-queue-admin logic, not a generic CRUD table.

Admin/on-call affordances: 'Live' poll indicator, a network banner with 'Retry now', monospace `code` styling for job ids, and the upload panel collapsed behind the header button so monitoring dominates the screen.

The visual skin is stock light-SaaS (Inter from Google Fonts, white cards on #f6f7f9, blue pill primary button, bottom-right toasts), so it stops short of the 'clearly driven type and color' bar — though the status-color system (red/blue/green/purple reused across cards, badges, and progress fills) is semantic rather than decorative.

Answered from idle_desktop before reading source — purpose: monitoring a background job queue ('Job Queue' h1, TOTAL/QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED count cards, jobs table, 'Live' dot). Matches the brief exactly.

Primary action: the solid blue 'Upload & Process' button is the only strong CTA (confirmed as primaryAction in metrics); at row level the yellow Retry buttons on failed rows are the obvious next action. Both readings are correct.

What needs attention: the red FAILED 3 card, three red Failed badges sorted to the top of the table, and red failure reasons ('Worker ran out of memory at 1.8 GB') each with an adjacent Retry — precisely the 'deal with failed jobs' half of the brief, obvious at a glance.
